# BCGov Crow - v0.16.0

## Release type

Minor release: new agent and skill.

## Summary

Added the Crow Data Architecture Agent and the `crow-data-architecture` skill
for relational data models on Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL with PostGIS,
and MySQL/MariaDB, using Entity Framework, JPA/Hibernate, Doctrine, or
Eloquent.

## Highlights

- Three routed modes: new model design, model changes for features and bug
  fixes, and large-scale refactoring during application modernization.
- Keep table and column descriptions, B.C. information security
  classifications (Public, Protected A, Protected B, Protected C), and
  ARCS/ORCS records schedules in the database. Records schedules are written
  as plain-text descriptions (records class title, retention period, and
  starting event) with the schedule number in brackets, so readers need no
  code lookup. Native storage is used where
  the engine supports it (SQL Server extended properties and sensitivity
  classification, Oracle 23ai annotations); elsewhere metadata is appended
  to the comment as a documented trailer.
- Verified provider guidance: Oracle EF Core comments are written through
  migration SQL because the provider emits `N'...'` comment literals, and
  Npgsql maps `[Timestamp] uint` to the PostgreSQL `xmin` concurrency token.
- Read, write, and validate bcgov/wwwsqldesigner `portable-v1` XML models,
  with a deterministic validator and a metadata SQL generator, both covered
  by tests.
- Hand-offs from application architecture, application development,
  solution architecture, and legacy modernization now route data modelling
  to the new agent.

## Scope and verification

The agent and skill are not added to the Starter Package or Security
Remediation collections. Full-package, plugin, and collection manifests are
aligned at 0.16.0. Asset, package, and release checks are required before
publication; final release verification and checksums remain pending.
